title: Essay Writing: Discursive, Argumentative and Reflective
summary: Planning and writing discursive, argumentative and reflective essays of 300–350 words: thesis, structure, counter-argument, cohesion, register and style.

notes.text: Grade 11 HL essays are usually **300–350 words**. Marks are given for **content and planning** (originality, depth of ideas), **language, style and editing** (register, word choice, sentence variety, accuracy) and **structure** (paragraphing, coherence).

rows: Persuade the reader to accept ONE view
Reasons for the stance; rebuts a counter-argument
Points for, then points against (or alternating)
Weighs both sides; may give a balanced view

notes.text: A reflective essay explores a personal experience, belief or idea and shows **insight**: what you learnt and how you changed. It is usually written in the first person, with honest, thoughtful language. Narrate only enough to support the reflection.

items: **Sentence variety**: mix short, punchy sentences with complex ones.
**Precise vocabulary**: 'detrimental' instead of 'bad'; 'scrutinise' instead of 'look at'.
**Register**: formal for argument; personal but controlled for reflection.

notes.title: Building a counter-argument paragraph
notes.problem: Topic: 'Social media does more harm than good.' (argumentative, agreeing)
steps: Concede: 'Admittedly, social media allows people to stay in touch with distant family.'
Rebut: 'However, studies of teenage users link heavy use to anxiety and poor sleep.'
Link: 'The benefits of connection are therefore outweighed by the damage to well-being.'
notes.answer: Concession + rebuttal + link makes the argument stronger and shows mature thinking.

notes.title: Avoiding repetition
notes.problem: Improve: 'The town was poor. The town had no clinic. The town needed help.'
notes.answer: 'The poor town had no clinic and it desperately needed help.'

questions.prompt: What is the usual length of a Grade 11 HL essay?
Which essay type explores both sides fairly?
Which essay type focuses on personal insight and growth?
An argumentative essay should state a clear stance in the introduction.
Mentioning a counter-argument always weakens an argumentative essay.
Match each discourse marker to its function.
Improve the vocabulary: 'The new law is really bad for poor people.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'The new legislation is detrimental to low-income households.' (precise, formal vocabulary) (2)

questions.prompt: Write a concession and rebuttal for an essay arguing that school should start at 9:00.
questions.memo:
✓ Concession of the opposing view, e.g. parents' work schedules (1)
✓ Rebuttal with a reason/evidence, e.g. teenagers' sleep needs and concentration (1)
✓ Appropriate discourse markers and formal register (1)

questions.prompt: Why should a reflective essay not simply tell a story?
questions.memo:
✓ The focus is on insight/meaning, not events (1)
✓ The writer must show what was learnt or how they changed (1)

questions.prompt: Write an introduction (2–3 sentences) for a discursive essay on 'Should matric exams be abolished?'
questions.memo:
✓ Introduces the issue engagingly (1)
✓ Indicates that both sides will be considered (1)
✓ Neutral, formal register (1)
